body:
Quick pass (reads only, not built) of head d9c799c13a1fc40396c49e961b494eeeb657e64b.

Result: pass

Not confirmed:
- The 23-step quick gate. The body states it. The quick pass did not re-run it.
- The test file `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_holes.rs` has no provenance line. A test is not a module, so this is minor.
- The style of the PR body was not checked sentence by sentence against ASD-STE100.

Checked:
- Head matches. GitHub reports `MERGEABLE` and `CLEAN` against main.
- The body is complete. It has the changes, the readings, the two pinning tests, the gate statement, the items not exercised, a `Changelog:` line and the closing line for #2431.
- No `unwrap()`, `expect(` or `panic!` in added source lines. The test file uses `expect` only in tests.
- The float math in `raster_bridge.rs:246-257` is checked. NaN fails the guard at line 249. The divisor `SPLIT_MZ` is a nonzero constant (`params.rs:302`).
- Provenance lines exist in `raster_bridge.rs:1-3` and `swarf.rs:1-2`. No "hsmworks" string appears in added lines.
- Line counts at head: `mod.rs` 130, `raster.rs` 305, `raster_bridge.rs` 90, `swarf.rs` 121. No file goes past 400 lines.
- The test file has a Gate map line that names `camcraft_motion::finishing3d`. Its imports resolve through `lib.rs:69-70`. No test is deleted or newly ignored. No golden file changed.
- The diff has no snapshot PNG, no `.github/` file, no process file and no new dependency. `docs/decisions/2431-parallel-over-holes.md` is present.
- No refusal, gouge check or collision check is removed. The new bridge adds a collision check (`raster_bridge.rs:238-272`). It tests all facets in the footprint padded by r (`support.rs:38-43`). The swarf move from `raster.rs` to `swarf.rs` reads as textually identical.

Read-only safety-floor review (Opus, diff only, not built) of head d9c799c13a1fc40396c49e961b494eeeb657e64b.

Verdict: findings, no blockers

What I checked:
- The gouge law in `bridge_ok` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/raster_bridge.rs:55-90`). The check uses the exact segment-to-triangle distance (`stock_sim::dist_seg_tri`, Ericson 5.1). It does not sample the feed, so the mesh detail cannot fall between samples. The check reads all facets from `build_sups`, not only the shallow facets. Thus walls beside the line, walls below the line, a step, and a pocket that is deeper on one side are all in the check. The bounding-box filter compares the segment box with the facet box padded by `r`. This filter is conservative: a facet that the swept ball can touch is never skipped.
- A tall step: I did the geometry for a plate piece that ends `r` before a wall of height `h`, with the next piece on the top. The segment comes within `r^2 / sqrt(r^2 + h^2)` of the wall edge, so the check refuses each real step. The pin `a_bridge_never_spans_a_wide_gap_or_a_tall_step` agrees.
- The tolerance sign. `limit = r - eps_chord` permits a bite of at most `eps_chord = min(tol/4, 0.005)`. This is the budget that the march spends on its own chords, and it is inside `DEV_TOL`. The sign is correct.
- Degenerate input. A zero gap makes a point segment, and `dist_seg_tri` falls back to the point distance. A NaN in `d`, `za`, `zb`, `tol` or `chord` makes a compare false, and the line keeps its break. `validate` refuses a zero or negative tool diameter. An empty mesh gives no lines, so the bridge does not run.
- No `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!` or index math in the new non-test code. `bridge_line` uses `first()`, `last()` and `last_mut()` with `let ... else` and `match`.
- `emit_runs` (`march.rs:345`) emits each pair of run points as one straight `Feed`. The certified segment is the motion that is posted.
- The swarf move. I compared the lines that `raster.rs` removes with the lines that `swarf.rs` adds. The bodies of `swarf` and `swarf_multi` are identical. Only the `use` lines and the provenance comment are new, and `rings_and_tail_with_trim` becomes `pub(super)`. There is no change of behaviour.
- No refusal or check is removed or made weaker. The bridge only joins pieces. It does not change `support_at`, `plunge_support` or the trim note.
- Code shape: `raster.rs` 305 lines, `raster_bridge.rs` 90, `swarf.rs` 121. The two new modules have a provenance comment. I found no clean-room problem.

Findings:
1. note - `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_holes.rs` (`deepest_bite` asserts): each test permits a bite up to `TOL` (0.05 mm). The code certifies a bite of at most `eps_chord` (0.0125 mm here). If a later change makes the limit `r - tol`, these tests stay green. Recommendation: assert `bite <= 0.25 * TOL` (or the `eps_chord` value plus a small sampling margin) in the bridge tests.
2. note - `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_holes.rs` (`a_bridge_never_spans_a_wide_gap_or_a_tall_step`): the name says "wide gap", but the test has only the 1 mm step. The wide gap is pinned by `a_hole_the_ball_fits_into_keeps_a_clean_hop`. A name change makes this clear.
3. note - test cover: all models are flat plates with axis-aligned walls, and only `FinishPattern::Parallel` runs. No test has a small hole in a sloped or curved surface, a blind slot narrower than `2r`, or the Scallop, blend or swarf patterns, which also go through `raster_pass_spaced`. The exact distance law makes a gouge there unlikely, but no test shows it. The PR body says this too.
4. note - `raster_bridge.rs:78`: when `r < eps_chord` (a tool diameter under 0.01 mm), `limit` is negative and the check always passes. The gap is then shorter than 0.01 mm, so the possible bite is very small. A `limit.max(0.0)` or a refusal for this case makes the law hold for each input.
5. note - `raster_bridge.rs:82-89`: each gap scans all facets. On a large mesh with many holes, this adds one pass over the facet list for each gap. `ball_clear` has the same cost for each sample, so this is not a new class of cost.

What I did not check:
- I did not build the change or run a test. I did not read the gate logs.
- I did not check the 5-axis orientation stamp of swarf over a bridged feed.
- I did not check how the app applies a machining boundary or containment after generation to a longer bridged feed.
- I did not check the overlap with PR #1713 (`gap_link`) after a merge.
